clue.text: See 14
Half of champagne covering one year

indicators.note: the champagne name wraps round, covering, the letter for one

parts.note: Moet is a famous brand of champagne
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Half a bottle of champagne sits over one year's celebrations.
explanation.definitionFit: A moiety is a formal or legal word for a half share or one of two parts.

clue.text: Change clubs for golf break

indicators.note: one letter standing for another signals a swap of letters in the word

parts.note: G is golf in the radio alphabet
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Swap your golf clubs during a break in play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs' and 'golf' look like the golfing picture; they are just the letters C and G.
explanation.definitionFit: A break, as in a lucky break, is an opportunity or chance to do something.

clue.text: Sticks to these stories going after drug with text message?

indicators.note: going after sends the stories piece behind the drug and message pieces

parts.note: ice is a slang name for crystal methamphetamine
LOL, laughing out loud, is a common text message
stories can mean untruths, lies

explanation.surface: Someone sticks to their tall tales after drugs and a jokey text.
explanation.walkthrough: Sticks looks like a verb but is the noun: these frozen treats are held on sticks, which is why the definition reads as it does.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice lollies are frozen fruit treats on wooden sticks, so sticks are attached to them; ice lolly is British for a popsicle.

clue.text: Queen holding award for one burnt in fire?

indicators.note: holding means the first piece contains the second

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen
an MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: The Queen hands over an award to a hero burnt in a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A glowing fragment left in a dying blaze is a coal that has been burnt in the fire.

clue.text: Recasts terrible performer

indicators.note: terrible suggests the word is badly mangled, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A director recasts a part because the performer was terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: An actress is a female performer on stage or screen.

clue.text: One to pour out wine for starters

parts.note: an means one, the indefinite article
to tip is to pour out a liquid
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to pour out wine before the starters arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasti are Italian appetisers served before the main meal, the first course.

clue.text: Tie up and hit hard

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a knot is a tie in rope or string

explanation.surface: Tie someone up and then beat them.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonk is British slang meaning to strike or thump something forcefully, as in batting.

clue.text: Model flips over label that's cut into curves

indicators.note: over means it goes round the next piece, enclosing it
flips means the word is turned back to front

parts.note: to pose is what a model does
to call is to label or name

explanation.surface: A fashion model somersaults over a garment label that has been cut into wavy edges.
explanation.walkthrough: Model is the verb, to strike an attitude, not a person; flips gives ESOP, which over then wraps round the label.
explanation.definitionFit: To escallop is to scallop, shaping an edge into a series of curved projections.

clue.text: No seats — full tours — fan sadly missing such events?

indicators.note: tours means goes round and about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, and removed from the pool

explanation.surface: A fan laments that every seat is gone and the tour is full, so they miss the concert.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffle NO SEATS FULL ('tours'); 'sadly missing' says the letters of FAN, rearranged, are taken out, leaving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigs with no tickets left are what the clue's preceding phrases describe, so 'such events' points to sold-out shows.

clue.text: See 17
Grounds cost Brad and Angelina in settlement

indicators.note: a divorce settlement rearranges the couple's assets, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A celebrity divorce settlement costs Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: COST BRAD and ANGELINA (16 letters, with and as a link) are shuffled; Grounds is the definition, not a legal reason.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanic gardens are landscaped grounds where plants are grown for study and display.

clue.text: Driving record and chart? Go off speed (acceleration for miles)

indicators.note: off means not right, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: for signals one letter taking another's place

parts.note: mph, miles per hour, measures speed
a is the physics symbol for acceleration

explanation.surface: A query about a driving record and chart, then an instruction to go off at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' shuffles CHART GO into TACHOGR; in MPH, A replaces M ('for') giving APH.
explanation.definitionFit: A tachograph is a device in lorries that records driving time and speed, a driver's log.

clue.text: French model Nicole stripped for casting?

indicators.note: casting means the letters are thrown into a new order
stripped means the outer letters are removed

explanation.surface: Nicole, a French model, strips off for a casting session.
explanation.walkthrough: In British TV adverts, Nicole was the French girl promoting the Renault car. 'stripped' leaves ICOL, which 'casting' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The Renault Clio is a small car made by a French manufacturer, so it is a French model of car.

clue.text: Who is one after "upping" vacuous policies to get elected?

definitions.text: Who is one after "upping" vacuous policies to get elected?

indicators.note: after places the doctor piece behind the others
upping, in a down clue, means reading those letters from the bottom upwards
vacuous means empty, so only the outer letters remain

parts.note: a party elected is said to be in
Doctor Who is the time-travelling hero of a BBC series, so Who is one doctor

explanation.surface: Who promotes empty policies so a party can win office?
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacuous' leaves P and S; 'upping' turns them to SP. The whole clue also describes a party's press manager.
explanation.definitionFit: A political press officer who puts a favourable gloss on hollow policies to help win elections fits the whole clue.

clue.text: Almost finish Tramp clue — hope cryptic device keeps some going

indicators.note: a cryptic arrangement is a puzzling, scrambled one, so the letters that follow are mixed up
almost the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written: the setter's name plus two plain words

explanation.surface: The setter Tramp hopes to complete a clue that keeps solvers going, like a machine sustaining a patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims FINISH to FINIS; 'cryptic' then shuffles FINIS with TRAMP CLUE HOPE into the 18-letter phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Hospital equipment that keeps critically ill patients alive by breathing or pumping for them is a device that keeps some going.

clue.text: Likely to let one go fast after puncture on bend

indicators.note: after sends the fasting piece behind the puncture and bend pieces

parts.note: a flat is a punctured tyre
a U-bend is a curved pipe, so U can stand for bend
Lent is the Christian period of fasting

explanation.surface: A cyclist goes fast after getting a puncture on a bend.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition uses slang: to let one go is to break wind, so the surface about a cyclist hides a rude joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone windy or gassy is liable to pass wind, the slang sense of letting one go.

clue.text: Inundated and embarrassed following speech, primarily; he brought Thatcher down

indicators.note: following puts the embarrassed piece after the rest
primarily means only the first letter is used

parts.note: Geoffrey Howe's 1990 resignation speech helped topple Margaret Thatcher
embarrassed people go red

explanation.surface: A politician, flooded with abuse and red-faced after a speech, is the man who brought Thatcher down.
explanation.walkthrough: Geoffrey Howe was a British Chancellor and Foreign Secretary whose resignation speech led to Margaret Thatcher's fall as Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Showered with gifts or praise means overwhelmed or flooded with them, so inundated.

clue.text: Ringer Enigmatist's tormented with pig

indicators.note: something tormented is twisted about, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written: the name of another crossword setter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fellow setter Enigmatist is pestered by a pig, perhaps a bell-ringer in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Enigmatist's is 'is', a link; ENIGMATIST plus PIG gives the thirteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringer is a person who looks exactly like someone else, a double or lookalike.

clue.text: Feature of 14 publicity around hard people

indicators.note: around means the first piece wraps the next

parts.note: hype is exaggerated publicity
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: A feature article on publicity surrounding a hard-nosed people.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 across, LIFE-SUPPORT, carries a hyphen, so the definition points to that entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The joining dash in the entry at 14 is a punctuation feature, the use of hyphens between word parts.

clue.text: Model supply for fine paper

parts.note: the Model T was an early Ford car
to issue is to supply or hand out

explanation.surface: A model maker asks for a supply of fine paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Tissue is thin, delicate paper used for wrapping or as a handkerchief.

clue.text: American guys, they deal with business

parts.note: gents are men, guys

explanation.surface: American men are the ones who handle business.
explanation.definitionFit: Representatives act on behalf of others in commercial dealings, handling business for clients.

clue.text: Using wife, husband after sex

indicators.note: after places the husband letter behind the sex piece

parts.note: it is a coy word for sex

explanation.surface: A marriage scenario: the wife, then the husband, after sex.
explanation.definitionFit: With can mean by means of, as in cutting with a knife, so using.

clue.text: Going Large on for couple grabbing space in Burger King?

indicators.note: for signals one pair of letters standing in for another

parts.note: the fast-food chain's name taken as written, run together
the pair of letters either side of the gap between the two words
taken as written

explanation.surface: Going Large on a meal deal at Burger King gets you a couple of extra portions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going Large' is Burger King's upsize option, here the definition. The letters hugging the space in BURGER KING are R and K; ON replaces them.
explanation.definitionFit: Burgeoning means growing rapidly or expanding, so going large in the literal sense.

clue.text: Weapon shortened by prisoner for prison

indicators.note: shortened means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a gun is a weapon
lag is slang for a convict, as in old lag

explanation.surface: A prisoner's weapon is cut down in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: The gulag was the Soviet system of forced labour camps, a prison.

clue.text: Greek character after fine food

indicators.note: after places the Greek letter behind the fine letter

parts.note: F is the pencil abbreviation for fine
eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek person enjoys good food after a fine meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is a white brined cheese from Greece, a foodstuff.

clue.text: Headless supporter is English — that man will cause trouble

indicators.note: headless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a bra is a supporting garment
he'll is the contraction of he will

explanation.surface: A headless English supporter is a troublemaker, like a football hooligan.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise hell is an idiom for making a great disturbance or fuss.

clue.text: Boxer and sucker: time for fresh start

indicators.note: a new first letter replaces the old one, so the initial is swapped

parts.note: a Dyson is a vacuum cleaner, a machine that sucks

explanation.surface: A boxer who is a sucker gets a new start.
explanation.walkthrough: Mike Tyson is the heavyweight boxer; the opening D gives way to T.
explanation.definitionFit: Mike Tyson was an undisputed world heavyweight champion fighter, an example of a boxer.

clue.text: Track box not on vehicle

parts.note: to dog is to track or follow

indicators.note: not means the following word is removed

parts.note: a carton is a box

explanation.surface: A tracking box isn't fitted to the vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Track' is a verb, follow, rather than a racing circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogcart is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage, a vehicle.
